tagline.text: A quiet white-sand island off Santa Cruz with a low-tide sandbar

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Maniwaya, Santa Cruz, Marinduque (offshore from Buyabod Port)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,000–4,500 (per person, 2 days and 1 night including round-trip transport from Manila)

children.text: Maniwaya Island is a small island off Santa Cruz in Marinduque, known for its long white-sand beach and the Palad sandbar that appears only at low tide. It is still lightly developed and a peaceful place to unwind.

Maniwaya Island lies in the Sibuyan Sea off the northeast of Marinduque and is both an island and a barangay under the municipality of Santa Cruz. Three large islands sit in the waters off Santa Cruz: Polo Island, the closest to the main island and ringed by mangroves; Mongpong Island, smaller and more mountainous; and Maniwaya, where the resorts are. Sources give its area as roughly
3–4 km²
, and it had a little over 1,500 residents in the 2020 census.

Its charm is simplicity. A long stretch of white sand, shallow clear water and an open shoreline for both sunrise and sunset are all there is, with no big hotels or shopping areas. It used to be home to just a few families, with Santa Cruz residents renting boats for a day by the sea and heading back before dark, but word of mouth led small resorts to open one by one. Local media have compared it to Boracay before it was developed.
About
1 km

off the northeastern tip of the island lies the Palad sandbar, roughly one hectare in size. Fine white sand is exposed only at low tide and disappears at high tide, and its shape changes with the season, currents and wind. An island-hopping trip combining this sandbar, the Ungab rock formation on Mongpong Island and a coral garden is the centerpiece of a visit to Maniwaya.
From Manila the trip takes about
6–9 hours

by road and boat, so a day trip is unrealistic and at least one night is best. There are no ATMs, credit cards are often not accepted and electricity is limited, but these inconveniences help keep the island quiet.

A small sandbar that appears in the middle of the sea at low tide, bright white. Timing your visit for the low tide in the early morning or late afternoon gives the best photos. In peak season boats can crowd it, and its shape differs each time.
Most of the island's resorts line the beach, so you can swim right in front of your lodging. It is a quiet shoreline where you can enjoy both sunrise and sunset.

A limestone rock formation on nearby Mongpong Island, usually included in island-hopping trips. When the sea is rough or during the habagat (southwest monsoon) season it may be hard to reach, so check conditions with your boatman first.
The shallow waters around the island have a coral garden where you can snorkel. Some areas may be closed for rehabilitation, so please follow your boatman's guidance.

A route that covers the sandbar, the Ungab rock and the coral garden in one trip. Renting one boat and splitting the cost with others keeps it affordable. If you are traveling alone, ask your resort whether you can join other guests.
Some resorts let you pitch a tent or rent a hammock, which makes the island popular with budget travelers. Spending a night on the beach to the sound of the waves is one of its great appeals.

According to local media, you can try jet skiing, banana boat rides, wakeboarding, kayaking and speedboats, and scuba diving is also available. This varies by operator and season, so check with your resort in advance.

items.title: 2-day, 1-night course
items.subtitle: From arrival on the island to a sandbar hopping trip

children.text: Take a Lucena-bound bus from Cubao, Buendia or elsewhere in Manila. An overnight bus gets you to Lucena around
, making it easier to catch the morning boat.
Take a van from Lucena Grand Terminal to General Luna, which takes about
2 hours
. Buy water and snacks at the terminal before leaving.
Arrive at General Luna, take a tricycle to the port and confirm the public boat to Maniwaya. Many guides say it departs once a day at
Arrive on the island, check in at your resort and drop your bags. Have lunch at the resort restaurant or one of the small shops on the beach.
Check the tide, then head out on an island-hopping trip. Snorkel at the Ungab rock and the coral garden, and stop at the Palad sandbar at low tide.
Watch the sunset from the beach and have dinner. Electricity is limited, so bring a flashlight and a power bank.
On day two, enjoy the sunrise and a walk along the beach. Reconfirm the return boat time with your resort and pack up.
On the way back, instead of heading straight to Manila you can also continue to explore the main island of Marinduque.

items.title: Marinduque combo course
items.subtitle: Sightseeing on the main island via Buyabod Port

children.text: Take the morning public boat from Maniwaya to Buyabod Port in Santa Cruz. Check the boat time with your resort each time.
Have breakfast in Santa Cruz town and look around the sights there, including the town church.
Head toward Boac by jeepney or van and visit other attractions on the main island of Marinduque.
At Balanacan Port, check the ferry to Dalahican in Lucena for the next day and wrap up your trip.

items.title: From Manila via Dalahican and Balanacan (Marinduque main island)

children.text: From Manila to Dalahican Port in Lucena by bus takes about
3–4 hours
, and the RORO ferry from the port to Balanacan Port in Marinduque takes about
3 hours
. Fares are listed at
depending on the vessel, and the terminal fee at Dalahican is around
From Balanacan to Santa Cruz by jeepney or UV van takes about
1 hour
, then a tricycle takes you to Buyabod Port.
The public boat from Buyabod Port to Maniwaya is said to run once or twice a day, in the morning and around midday, taking about
30–45 minutes
and costing around
per person. If you miss it, chartering costs between
JAC Liner and others sometimes run through buses that include the ferry from Buendia or Cubao in Manila, taking about
7–8 hours
in total.
This route suits travelers who want to see the main island of Marinduque first. There are many transfers, so allow extra time.
Cebu Pacific (Cebgo) began direct flights from Manila to Marinduque Airport (Gasan) in April 2019, and the flight takes about
1 hour
or less. Days and availability vary by period, so check the latest schedule.
From the airport you travel overland to Santa Cruz and then take a boat from Buyabod Port.
The island is small and most travel is on foot. The resorts are strung along the beach.
Trips beyond the island, such as hopping and the sandbar, are done by chartering a boat through your resort or a boatman.
March–May, when the sea is calm and the skies are clear, is the best time. December–February is also dry and relatively cool, so it is a good time to travel. Guides generally recommend November–June.

In June–August the habagat (southwest monsoon) raises waves and boats may be cancelled, and September–October is the rainy and typhoon season, best avoided. How much of the Palad sandbar shows depends on the tide, so check the tide table before you visit.

Resorts reported on the island have included Wawie's Beach Resort, Playa Amara, Residencia De Palo Maria and Marikit na Beach Resort. Options range widely from tents and hammocks to fan rooms and air-conditioned rooms, and are generally simple. Names and rates can change, so before booking be sure to ask whether boat transfers, island hopping and meals are included.

Meals are taken at resort restaurants and small shops on the beach. Seafood is often cooked to order, and choices of restaurants and shops are limited. It is a good idea to buy water and snacks in advance in General Luna or Lucena. Some reviews say power comes from generators and is supplied only in the evening at many places, so it is safer to assume you cannot run air-conditioning all night.
There are no ATMs on the island and many places do not accept cards. Bring plenty of cash, mostly in small bills.
To avoid missing the General Luna public boat, many travelers plan to leave Manila around midnight.
Check the tide and visit the sandbar early in the morning or late in the afternoon for the best experience.
Bring a waterproof pouch, aqua shoes, reef-safe sunscreen, insect repellent and a power bank.
Weekends, Holy Week and holidays are crowded, so weekdays are recommended.
Reconfirm the return boat time with your resort the night before.
If you are alone or in a small group, ask your resort to arrange a joined hopping trip so you can share the cost.
Mobile signal can be weak or unreliable, so save your itinerary and booking details in advance.
There are only one or two public boats a day, so missing one makes chartering expensive. The Coast Guard may suspend boat trips in bad weather, so check the weather and the latest announcements.
Electricity, fresh water and signal are limited and there is no large pharmacy. Bring your own basic medicines.
Boat cancellations and schedule changes are frequent during habagat and typhoon season, so avoid tight schedules just before your flight home.
Parts of the coral may be under rehabilitation, so do not step on or touch it, and take your trash with you.
Fares and timetables differ between guides and change often. Check the latest information with your resort and at the pier before departure.
The sandbar is submerged by the rising tide, so do not stay long without knowing the tide.
The whole island that Maniwaya belongs to, with attractions such as the Moriones Festival and Boac. It connects overland after about
30 minutes
by boat.
The capital of Marinduque, with its cathedral and old town. Reached overland from Santa Cruz.
A transit city on the way from Manila, with Dalahican Port and bus terminals.
A neighboring island with the Ungab rock formation, usually included in hopping trips.
